subject: Follow-up: Lumina Health — network boundaries & on‑prem requirements
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Cole <sara.cole@luminahealth.ai>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@luminahealth.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: Lumina Health — network boundaries & on‑prem requirements

Hi Sara / Jorge,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful context. Below is a concise recap of the pain you described, the goals we heard, and the concrete next steps we agreed to. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Quick recap (pain / drivers)
- Regulatory/data residency: PHI and provincial patient records must remain in Canadian infrastructure; company policy requires avoidance of cross-border PHI egress.
- Network hardening: No outbound internet egress from production environment except via explicit allow-listed endpoints; IDS/IPS and strict firewall rules.
- Air‑gap/staging requirement: Staging environment must be air-gapped for vulnerability testing and some vendor validation windows.
- Audit and key control: Need KMS integration with BYOK/HSM and immutable audit logs forwarded to Splunk.

Goals we discussed
- Proof-of-concept: Private deployment (VPC or on‑prem) for a small model serving footprint to validate performance and compliance.
- Timebox: 6–8 week POC if network and security gating items look straightforward.
- Success criteria: SLOs for 95th percentile latency < 200 ms for baseline prompts, no PHI leaving Canadian tenancy, and collection of audit logs into your Splunk instance.

Technical constraints you flagged
- Required static egress IPs for allow-listing with your network team.
- Mutual TLS for all control-plane API calls; client certs managed by Lumina’s PKI.
- Port restrictions: only outbound HTTPS (443) allowed from the compute subnet; some tunnels for private connectivity (IPsec) may be required.
- VPC peering vs. transit architecture: you prefer peering into a dedicated subnet in your VPC rather than exposing internet routes.

Attachments (attached with this email)
- Lumina_vpc_requirements.xlsx — high-level template for network items we discussed (IP ranges, owners, required ports).

Next steps (agreed)
1) You to share a network diagram and point of contact on the infra/security side (Jorge noted he will own).
2) We’ll produce a short technical runbook and a pared-down architecture sketch for a Canada-hosted private deployment (aim: 48–72 hours after we get the diagram).
3) SE review call w/ your infra & security teams next week (requesting a 60-minute slot).
4) We’ll propose a POC schedule and an initial list of static IPs and mTLS cert flow for allow-listing.

If this looks right I’ll loop in our Solutions Engineering lead (Ava) and Marcus (technical account lead) to begin the runbook and IP list.

Thanks — talk soon,

--
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0182

[Attachment: Lumina_vpc_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 28 KB)]

From: Sara Cole <sara.cole@luminahealth.ai>

Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@luminahealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 19:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Lumina Health — network boundaries & on‑prem requirements

Thanks Nikhil — this is a great summary and captures the key points. A few clarifications and additional constraints from our security team: 

Clarifications
- Data residency: All PHI must remain in Canada at rest and in transit. We have an AWS Canada (Central) tenancy preferred for any cloud-hosted option.
- Staging air-gap: For 3rd party vendor assessments we require a true air‑gapped staging environment (no outbound egress) for up to 48 hours during audits.

Additional requirements
- KMS/BYOK: Customer-managed keys are mandatory for production. Ideally integrate with our existing AWS KMS HSM-backed keys.
- Logging: We need the option to forward audit logs and API traces to our Splunk collector over a dedicated log-forwarding tunnel; logs must be immutable for 1 year.
- Identity: Okta SAML for admin console access; SCIM for provisioning.

Network owners/contact
- Jorge Ramos (Infra) — jorge.ramos@luminahealth.ai (he’ll share the network diagram and firewall policy).

I’ve attached a rough network diagram and a preliminary matrix of flows we anticipate — Jorge will update with CIDRs. Also can you confirm whether Redwood supports an on‑prem bundle (appliance/container) we could run in our data center if the cloud route proves infeasible?

Sara
--
Sara Cole
Director, IT Security | Lumina Health
sara.cole@luminahealth.ai

Hi all — quick confirmation from infra side. We received your attachment and will populate CIDRs by end of day tomorrow. A couple follow-ups we need from Redwood to scope the POC properly: 

1) Static IPs: please provide a preliminary list of egress/static IPs (or range) we can begin to allow-list for the POC. If you don’t have fixed IPs, advise intended approach (NATed egress vs. dedicated peering).
2) Certificate flow: we need hardware-backed client certs for control-plane mTLS — can Redwood accept certs signed by our internal CA?
3) On‑prem option: please share the packaging format (Docker images + Helm chart or a VM appliance) plus minimum host specs (GPU/CPU/memory) and offline install guide.

Timeline ask from Lumina: we’d like a proposed POC timeline and rough cost estimate for the POC (engineering hours + any infra uplift) so leadership can green-light the procurement.

We’ll upload the network diagram update and firewall ACL draft to the Drive link Sara included.

Thanks,
Jorge
